Context/Background: ASXL1 plays key roles in epigenetic regulation of early developmental gene expression. De novo protein-truncating mutations in ASXL1 cause Bohring-Opitz syndrome (BOS), a rare neurodevelopmental condition characterized by severe intellectual disabilities, distinctive facial features, hypertrichosis, increased risk of Wilms tumor, and variable congenital anomalies, including heart defects and severe skeletal defects giving rise to a typical BOS posture. These BOS-causing ASXL1 variants are also high-prevalence somatic driver mutations in acute myeloid leukemia.  We used primary cells from individuals with BOS (n = 18) and controls (n = 49) to dissect gene regulatory changes caused by ASXL1 mutations using comprehensive multiomics assays for chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), DNA methylation, histone methylation binding, and transcriptome in peripheral blood and skin fibroblasts.
Prompt: Based on the results of the blood and fibroblast transcriptomic DEG analyses of BOS vs controls, provide a discussion of the common and distinct pathways found between blood and fibroblast and any relevance to the presence in the BOS samples of ASXL1 truncating mutations.

Introduction/Context  
ASXL1 truncating mutations underlie Bohring-Opitz syndrome (BOS), a severe neurodevelopmental disorder. Here, RNA-seq in primary skin fibroblasts (n = 18 BOS, 49 controls) and peripheral blood (n = 18 BOS, 49 controls) identified differentially expressed genes. Fibroblasts showed 999 DEGs (padj < 0.05); blood showed 2,118 DEGs (padj < 0.05). Definitive signals: fibroblasts—upregulated neuronal guidance programs and downregulated PI3K-Akt signaling and immune modules; blood—broad suppression of inflammatory/cytokine pathways and upregulation of select developmental, heme-scavenging, and complement modules. Details not specified: age distribution, sex breakdown.

Balanced analysis (4–8 sentences)  
Across both tissues, ASXL1 truncation associates with suppression of immune/inflammatory modules (e.g., downregulation of “Immune System,” “Inflammatory Response,” cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction) and activation of neurodevelopmental programs (e.g., “Nervous System Development,” “Axon Guidance”). Fibroblasts uniquely exhibit downregulated PI3K-Akt signaling, suggesting altered survival/growth signaling, whereas blood shows robust downregulation of phagosome and neutrophil degranulation pathways alongside upregulation of heme-scavenging and complement cascades. The predominance of neuronal guidance genes (CNTN4) in fibroblasts likely reflects ASXL1’s epigenetic role in early developmental gene control; conversely, the hematopoietic context reveals immune dysregulation consistent with ASXL1’s known involvement in myeloid malignancy. Distinct pathway dysregulation underscores tissue-specific chromatin contexts modulating ASXL1’s impact, with shared themes of immune attenuation and developmental misexpression.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtering by “PI3K-Akt,” “Axon,” and “Cytokine” retrieves key terms:  
– PI3K-Akt signaling (fibroblast, down)  
– Axon Guidance, Axonogenesis, Neuron Projection Guidance (fibroblast, up)  
– Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction (blood, down)  
– Inflammatory Response (blood, down)  
This confirms our focus on developmental and immune pathways as central ASXL1-linked mechanisms.

Comparisons  
– Concordant: Both tissues suppress immune and inflammatory arms (higher confidence shared phenotype).  
– Fibroblast-specific: PI3K-Akt down, axon-related up (reflects non-hematopoietic epigenetic impacts).  
– Blood-specific: pronounced neutrophil function and cytokine signaling suppression, plus complement activation (reflects ASXL1’s hematopoietic driver role).  

Implications  
ASXL1 truncations perturb chromatin at enhancers governing developmental (axonogenesis) and immune gene loci, yielding tissue-specific transcriptomic footprints. In fibroblasts, misexpression of neuronal guidance genes could underlie congenital skeletal/neural anomalies. In blood, immune dysregulation aligns with BOS patients’ leukemia risk, suggesting that early inflammatory suppression may predispose to clonal expansion.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Integrate ATAC-seq/histone-mark profiles to map ASXL1-regulated enhancers at CNTN4 and PI3K-Akt loci.  
2. Validate PI3K-Akt signaling perturbation by Western blot of p-AKT in fibroblasts.  
3. Assess immune cell subpopulations in BOS blood to clarify the cellular basis of inflammatory suppression.  
4. Clarify whether “epigenetic regulation” GO terms emerge at relaxed thresholds (currently not observed under padj < 0.05).
